newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Hostages flee Mindanao fighting, rebel camp falls.
newsitem.headline: Hostages flee Mindanao fighting, rebel camp falls.

text.p: Nearly 50 bus passengers taken hostage by Moslem rebels on Thursday dashed to freedom during a gun battle and a major guerrilla camp fell in an army offensive in the southern Philippines, the military said.

At least seven people, including a civilian, died in a battle between the rebels and soldiers on a country road near Cotabato city after Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF) rebels stopped a convoy of buses passing through the area, it said.
MILF vice chairman Ghazali Jaafar said the rebels had decided to indefinitely postpone Saturday's scheduled exploratory peace talks with the government in view of the renewed fighting.
"It is our conviction that the atmosphere is not conducive to the peace talks," Jaafar said in a letter to the government.
Army spokesman Captain Noel Detoyato said soldiers were conducting clearing operations to see if the rebels had taken any other hostages with them in their retreat.
But 47 had broken free of the guerrillas, he said.
The MILF suffered a further blow when soldiers occupied Camp Rajamuda, the rebels' second biggest base on Mindanao island, hours after the rebels abandoned it, Detoyato said.
"We have hoisted the Philippine flag over it," he said.
He said the loss of the camp, which the MILF had used as a launching pad for its operations in nine nearby towns, deprived them of a major sanctuary and logistics source.
Jaafar said he was still awaiting word from Rajamuda and that soldiers might have occupied only the camp's perimeter.
"This is not yet over. Our forces are just re-positioning," he told Reuters by telephone.
"We ran for our lives when the soldiers arrived and shooting started," said Grace Cadungog, one of the passengers who fled as the gunfire broke out.
"One of the gunmen said, 'shoot them', but another one said, 'Don't, let them go'," Cadungog said.
Jaafar denied the MILF took hostages. He said the rebels stopped buses at a blockade they had set up to prevent an army advance, and trouble erupted when soldiers opened fire.
The seven killed included four guerrillas, two soldiers and one of the bus passengers, the military said.
The military said at least 45 people, mostly rebels, had died and more than 30,000 villagers had fled their homes in more than a week of fighting.
The MILF, with an estimated 8,000 armed fighters, is battling for independence for Mindanao, the ancestral Moslem homeland in the predominantly Christian Philippines.
